transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been dealing with constant, uncontrollable worry about almost everything in my life, from my work and family to our finances. I just can't seem to stop it, and this has been going on for about two years and four months now.
Besides the constant worry, have you also been experiencing a persistent low mood or a loss of interest in activities that you used to enjoy for most of these past two years?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling depressed or lost interest in my hobbies. My main struggle is really just this constant, overwhelming worry that I can't seem to turn off. I still want to do things, but the anxiety and "what-ifs" just completely take over.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denies symptoms of low mood or anhedonia, which makes Major Depressive Disorder and Persistent Depressive Disorder unlikely. The clinical presentation of chronic, uncontrollable worry lasting over two years strongly points toward Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
